blocks.name: Program Requirements

rules.name: Core Seminar
rules.desc: The Philosophy, Literature, and the Arts Core Seminar is team-taught by faculty from philosophy and a literature or arts department.

rules.name: Two Additional Courses
rules.desc:
Two additional courses at the 200 level or above deemed by the Committee in Charge to include material of substantial special relevance to the domain of philosophy, literature, and the arts.
At least one of these courses should be offered in a participating department other than the student’s major department (e.g., a philosophy course for students in literature and arts departments, a literature or arts course for philosophy students).

rules.name: Two Minor Field Courses
rules.desc:
All students take two graduate-level courses providing a structured program of coursework in the student’s minor field (such as philosophy for literature and arts students or literary or arts criticism for philosophy students):

• Graduate students in Philosophy take two graduate-level courses in a single literature or one of the arts.

• Graduate students in literature or arts departments, including Classics, take two graduate-level courses in Philosophy, at least one of which must be in metaphysics, epistemology, or the philosophies of language, mind, or action (the PHIL 280s series and related upper-level seminars), and at least one of which must be in value theory (understood to include ethics, aesthetics, and political philosophy, the PHIL 270s series and related upper-level seminars)

• Graduate students in other departments submit a plan of study for approval by the Faculty Director reflecting graduate-level coursework that provides a background both within philosophy and within the study of literature or the arts that is substantially equivalent to that achieved by philosophy, literature, or arts students in their minor field. Students are advised that this study plan may involve more coursework than would be needed for students whose major field is in literature, arts, or philosophy departments.

rules.name: Optional Remaining Units
rules.desc: If the five required courses do not total 20 units, students may satisfy the 20-unit requirement by taking units of DLCL 222,or by taking additional graduate-level courses of special relevance at their discretion and with the agreement of their minor advisor.

rules.name: Other graduate courses toward the 20 units, agreed with your minor advisor

blocks.notes:
Notes:
Students are encouraged to include a member from the minor field on the University Oral Committee or another of the general examination committees if that is judged more appropriate by the student’s departmental and minor advisors. Students in departments that deploy the University Oral as a dissertation defense are advised that a member from the student’s minor field should be involved on the dissertation committee throughout the dissertation writing period.

reviewNotes: You take the core seminar DLCL 333, two more courses from the list (at least one should be in a participating department other than your own), and two graduate courses in your minor field, for at least 20 units in all. Which minor-field courses count depends on your home department, so you move them in by hand. If the five courses come to fewer than 20 units, DLCL 222 units count toward the total, and other graduate courses your minor advisor agrees to can be moved in by hand.
